A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and can be matched across the revision.

before.justification: V2 reports original compression benchmarks, sparsity sweeps, weight-importance analyses, and selective-quantization experiments, including Tables 1–4.

after.justification: V3 retains these original experiments and adds annotation validation, AlphaPruning evaluations, non-R1 experiments, retrieval-assisted evaluation, and further diagnostic results.

M1.justification: The steering-vector computation, attribution-patching importance scores, relative-importance normalization, and selective final-layer protection procedure remain unchanged. V3 applies this framework to additional models and compression settings without introducing a new proposed algorithm.

E1.justification: The four reasoning benchmarks are retained. Appendix L adds an actually evaluated retrieval-assisted MuSiQue scenario, supplying external knowledge to the models; v2 evaluates MuSiQue only closed-book and references other work's RAG results.

E2.justification: V3 adds AlphaPruning to Table 1 for R1-Distill-Llama-70B at 50% sparsity and Llama-8B at 30% and 50%. The previous comparator set remains; rows formerly labeled 'sparse' are identified explicitly as SparseGPT.

E3.justification: V3 adds substantial evaluation designs: annotation validation at temperatures 1 and 0.1, a GPT-OSS-distilled 4B model with its GPTQ variant, retrieval-assisted MuSiQue, and selective 4-/5-bit Llama and 3-bit Qwen tests. Existing benchmark sizes and generation settings remain unchanged; the newly disclosed 120-instance annotation dataset does not establish a revised sampling protocol.

E4.justification: New Appendices G–N investigate annotation stability, dependence on displaying only importance decreases, pruning effects, non-R1 generalization, base-model importance, knowledge provision through RAG, agreement with AWQ scaling signals, and the first-versus-final-layer quantization exception. These substantially extend validation of the central findings. V2's response-length analysis and collapse cases remain in Appendices O/P.

E5.justification: Appendix G and Table 6 introduce Spearman correlations and 95% confidence intervals for human annotation ratings, using ten instances sampled with replacement per behavior. This statistical reporting is localized to annotation validation; existing benchmark averaging and one-pass sparsity reporting remain unchanged.

E6.justification: Existing numerical entries in Tables 1–4 and the relocated response-length tables are unchanged. V3 adds AlphaPruning results, annotation ratings, non-R1 scores, RAG outcomes, and selective-quantization results. For example, Table 7 reports average accuracies of 71.1 and 63.2 for DistilGPT-OSS-qwen3-4B and its 4-bit GPTQ variant; Table 8 reports Llama-8B MuSiQue F1 of 4.43 closed-book versus 14.52 with RAG.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and equations for steering vectors, attribution importance, and relative importance are retained, as is the minimal-importance-shift hypothesis. V3 adds empirical validation and conceptual explanations, without new formal results, proofs, or derivations.

C1.justification: The abstract and conclusion broaden the three headline findings from R1-distilled Llama/Qwen models to R1 and non-R1 families. The introduction and conclusion also extend the excessive-compression finding to pruning, expanding the claimed mechanistic contribution beyond distillation and quantization. The original headline numerical gains remain unchanged.

C2.justification: V3 adds substantive interpretations of RAG gains, model-specific importance patterns, pruning-analysis feasibility, and the selective-quantization exception, which it attributes to random perturbation. It also discusses hardware tradeoffs of nonuniform compression, unmatched dynamic-quantization calibration, and uncertainty from the small annotation-validation sample.

D1.justification: Documentation expands substantially: v3 specifies the 120 annotated instances with 30 per benchmark, annotation temperature and sequence exclusions, component-specific precision in the dynamically quantized model, and calibration-information limitations. It also documents AlphaPruning's use of SparseGPT and the RAG embedding model and top-ten retrieval procedure. Existing code-access information remains unchanged.

R1.justification: New Appendix B.5 positions the importance analysis within module-wise compression, adding AlphaPruning, OWL, and Liu et al.'s principal-weight study. This is a targeted extension of the retained literature review and research positioning. OWL is discussed but not evaluated as a baseline.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and the main section sequence are retained. V3 makes local wording corrections, adds cross-references, acknowledgments, and conference headers, and inserts new appendix sections. The former Appendices G/H become O/P with their substantive text preserved.

P2.justification: V3 substantially expands the displays with new validation and evaluation tables and importance heatmaps in Figures 8–13. Figure 2 is enlarged and rearranged into stacked groups, and Figure 1 incorporates AlphaPruning. Existing response-length tables and the collapse illustration are relocated and renumbered, with their content retained.

improvement.justification: V2 explicitly omitted mechanistic pruning analysis and lacked annotation-validation and non-R1 checks. V3 adds these, together with base-model and selective-quantization controls that substantially strengthen the central weight-importance argument. These additions address important validation gaps. The annotation sample remains small, and RAG comparisons do not fully isolate knowledge from reasoning, so some strengthened generalization and causal interpretations remain insufficiently supported.
